text: Semen for cattle AI is collected from bulls of high genetic value — using selected sires can improve meat production capacity in the offspring of local cattle. Semen is stored in straws submerged in liquid nitrogen tanks, held at -196°C, allowing storage for months or years. Once a cow is detected in estrus, AI should be performed 12 to 24 hours later, with 18 hours after detection being the ideal timing. Only trained technicians should inseminate cattle: a straw is removed from the tank and warmed to ambient temperature to 'wake up' the sperm; the technician performs a rectal exam with one hand to locate and hold the cervix, then introduces the semen straw through the vagina and cervix with the other hand using a specialized catheter (called a 'gun') to deposit the dose in the uterus.
